blocks.text: Born in 1987 and based in Gunma Prefecture, Japan, Mari Katayama makes self-portraits, hand-sewn objects and soft sculptures in which her own body sits alongside the things she assembles. She always presses the shutter herself, and she favors materials available to everyone, convinced that needle and thread are the strongest tools. Her work questions assumptions about what is natural, artificial or expected of a body. In 2022, Tate acquired her self-portrait “bystander #23” (2016), which went on view at Tate Modern the following year.

This video is a short documentary produced by Tate, “Art should be for everyone.” Katayama describes her creative process, her need for a quiet place to work, and why, in her view, art belongs to everyone, whatever materials are used.
10 minutes, in Japanese with English subtitles.
